Definition: from G3650 and G2819; complete in every part, i.e. perfectly sound (in body):--entire, whole.
BiblicalUsage: holóklēros means entire, whole. It turns up twice, in 1 Thessalonians and James.
TheologicalSignificance: I take holóklēros as it stands — entire, whole — and read the passage with that plain sense in mind.
